concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a business transaction is an exchange of economic consideration with a give and a take aspect recorded in at least two accounts.
Identify source documents such as cash memo, invoice, pay-in-slip and cheque as evidence on which all recording is based.
Distinguish transaction, debit, credit and journal (complex) vouchers by the number of debits and credits involved.
State the essential elements an accounting voucher must contain and how long vouchers are preserved.
State the accounting equation A = L + C and use its derived forms to find a missing figure.
Analyse the effect of transactions on assets, liabilities and capital and show that the equation stays balanced.
Describe the T-account and explain that debit means the left side and credit the right side of an account.
Apply the rules of debit and credit to assets, liabilities, capital, expenses and revenues.

topics.title: Books of Original Entry and the Journal

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the journal as the book of original entry and the purpose of its columns, narration and L.F.
Record simple and compound journal entries for transactions involving two or more accounts.
Record journal entries for purchases and sales under CGST, SGST and IGST and compute net GST payable after set-off.

topics.title: The Ledger and Posting from Journal

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the ledger as the principal book and distinguish it from the journal.
Classify ledger accounts into permanent accounts and temporary accounts.
Describe the steps of posting journal entries to the debit and credit sides of ledger accounts.
